clue.text: In Paris, I've left prison

blocks.note: French for 'I have' is j'ai
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone announces that, while in Paris, they walked out of prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' tells you to translate the next word into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail is a straightforward synonym for a prison, a place of lawful confinement.

clue.text: Time in piece of music satisfactory for composer

indicators.note: in places the time abbreviation inside the joined musical piece and the word for satisfactory

blocks.note: a bar is a short measured section of a piece of music
T is the abbreviation for time
OK means acceptable or satisfactory

explanation.surface: A judgement that the timing in some piece of music is good enough for its composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The time letter goes inside the two following pieces once they are joined, landing between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer, so he is an example of the defining class.

clue.text: Decline shortest article or long story

blocks.note: to sag is to droop or decline
of the articles a, an and the, A is the shortest

explanation.surface: A choice between cutting an article right down or letting it run on at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortest article' is the grammatical article, not a newspaper piece: A is the shortest of a, an and the.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally a Norse tale of heroes, now any lengthy story.

clue.text: A female in Asian garment for trip after big game

indicators.note: in tells you the first two pieces sit inside the garment

blocks.note: a sari is a draped garment worn by women in South Asia
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman in a sari setting off on an expedition to hunt large animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition, typically in Africa, to hunt or watch large wild animals, which hunters call big game.

clue.text: Least sensible part of job armies tackled

indicators.note: the answer is only a portion of the following words, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of job, through armies and into tackled

explanation.surface: The silliest bit of the work that the armed forces took on.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy is British slang for foolish or mad, so its superlative means the least sensible.

clue.text: Greek character on a strange mission — very hush-hush?

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek person off on an odd assignment that is extremely secret.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the rest. The question mark flags that 'very hush-hush' is meant musically, not as secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pianissimo is the musical direction for playing very quietly, which is a playful sense of being very hushed.

clue.text: Area set in Siam, possibly, or another Eastern country

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the preceding word is rearranged
the first pair of pieces sits inside the rearranged word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
A is the abbreviation for area
to lay something is to set it down

explanation.surface: Pointing to a region located in Siam, or else some other country of the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Siam (now Thailand) is itself an Eastern country, which is why the definition says 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaysia is a nation of South-East Asia, a different country from Siam but in the same region.

clue.text: Got off course, so remained without some basic education

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: to stay is to remain
R is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: Someone wandered off the path and so stayed behind with no schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside. The three Rs are the basics of schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander from the proper route, so strayed means went off course.

clue.text: Saw cut one circle in slow movement

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the preceding word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a saw is an old saying, an adage
I is the Roman numeral one
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone sawed out a ring while moving very slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool or a past tense, but it is a noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a piece or movement played at a slow tempo, from Italian for 'at ease'.

clue.text: Irish quarter changed as result

indicators.note: something changed is altered in form, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Part of Ireland was transformed as a consequence of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, so one quarter of the island.

clue.text: Preparing to fight outside US city — that's scary

indicators.note: outside tells you the first word wraps around the second

blocks.note: arming is equipping oneself for battle
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: People taking up weapons just beyond an American city, which is frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming causes fear or worry, so it is scary.

clue.text: Misbehaviour of king in banking, for example

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the longer phrase

blocks.note: banking is one example of a money business
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king behaving badly within the world of banking.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for mischievous or dishonest behaviour.

clue.text: Vessel in evident trouble listed, finally capsized

indicators.note: finally points to the end letter of each of the two words before it
in puts the vessel inside the remaining letters

blocks.note: overt means plainly evident
an urn is a vase or vessel
the last letters of trouble and listed

explanation.surface: A ship in clear difficulty leaned over and in the end turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a sea disaster, but 'vessel' is a pot and 'listed' just supplies its end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that has overturned has been turned over in the water, which is what capsized means.

clue.text: Like book that's complete, or marginally unfinished

blocks.note: first meaning: unabridged, with nothing removed
second meaning: of a book whose page edges have not been trimmed

explanation.walkthrough: In bookbinding, a book with untrimmed page edges is called uncut, so it is unfinished at the margins.
explanation.definitionFit: An unabridged text has had nothing cut, and untrimmed pages have literally had their margins left uncut by the binder.

clue.text: Conclusions reached by student despite the chaos in places on course

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so only the final letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: the last letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A pupil comes to final decisions in spite of the disorder around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a golf course, not a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Tees are the marked areas on a golf course from which each hole is begun.

clue.text: Mass movement suddenly made an impression on European

blocks.note: to stamp is to press a mark or impression into something
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A sudden surge of people made a strong impact on someone from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of a herd or crowd, a mass movement that happens all at once.

clue.text: Cut diamonds right, left, and centre

indicators.note: one reading of the word goes at both sides and the other reading goes in the middle

blocks.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds, used once on each side
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Gems being cut everywhere you look.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'diamonds' is read twice: as the card suit D at right and left, and as the slang ICE in the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Diced food has been cut into small cubes, so diced is a past participle meaning chopped.

clue.text: Stump, perhaps, as part of crossword is missing

indicators.note: the answer is just a portion of the words that follow, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of crossword, through is and into missing

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled because a bit of the puzzle has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a wicketkeeper stumps a batsman by breaking the wicket while they are out of their ground; it is one way to get them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumping is one method of dismissing a batsman, so to stump is an example of to dismiss.

clue.text: Mostly perform brain operations fine

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: thinking is what the brain does

explanation.surface: A surgeon mostly doing fine work on brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brain operations' suggests surgery, but it just means mental activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin and fine both describe something of small thickness, like a fine or thin thread.

clue.text: Result of shocking event at sanatorium? It might be

indicators.note: might be hints the letters could form something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether someone in a sanatorium is there because of some terrible shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Traumatisation is the state of psychological injury that follows a deeply distressing experience.

clue.text: Leaders abandoning PM and his very hapless state

indicators.note: the leading letters walk away, so each word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: PM without its first letter
his without its first letter
very without its first letter

explanation.surface: Party chiefs desert the Prime Minister, leaving him in a truly sorry position.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is the Prime Minister. 'And' only joins the pieces, so it is not trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Misery is great unhappiness, a wretched and unlucky condition to be in.

clue.text: First-class spinner following bit of advice

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the spinner is placed behind the advice

blocks.note: a tip is a helpful hint
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A top-class spin bowler acting on some advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, but here it is the child's toy. 'Following' puts it after the hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top is an informal term for excellent, of the highest quality.

clue.text: Offer support, also reforms

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it anew, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a prop is a support
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician offers backing and also promises changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for consideration, an offer such as a plan or marriage proposal.

clue.text: Family endlessly raised capital

indicators.note: with no ends, so both the first and last letters are removed
raised in a down clue means lifted upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A family without end has raised money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Something from abroad the writer's left on plane

blocks.note: the writer is 'I', and 'the writer's' is I'm, I is
port is the left-hand side of an aircraft or ship

explanation.surface: A traveller left something from overseas behind on the aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the writer is the setter, I, so 'the writer's' becomes I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: An import is a good brought in from a foreign country.

clue.text: Read note, oddly, as expression of anger

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in odd-numbered positions: first, third and so on

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone reads a message, strangely enough, as a sign of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A rant is a loud, angry tirade, a way of expressing fury.

clue.text: Sensitive and caring type

blocks.note: first meaning: sore or easily hurt
second meaning: a person who tends or looks after something

explanation.surface: Describing a person who is delicate and also looks after others.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender is an adjective for something painful to touch, and a noun for one who tends, such as a bartender or carer.

clue.text: Reckoning error I found in manuscript is by Tolstoy, say

indicators.note: something found in another is located inside it

blocks.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript
taken as written
Leo Tolstoy held the title of count, a nobleman

explanation.surface: A scholar spots an error in a manuscript that turns out to be Tolstoy's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By Tolstoy' suggests authorship, but 'by' just sets the nobleman beside the other pieces; Tolstoy was a count.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscount is a mistake in counting, an error in reckoning up a total.
